bugs.finding_type: Misuse of `system` function in runCommand method. The system() call is dangerous as it can execute any command passed to the parameter, which could lead into a buffer overflow or other security issue if not properly sanitized and validated inputs are provided by users for this purpose (like user-provided commands).
bugs.description: `system` function in C++ has been deprecated. It is recommended that you use Popen() instead to execute the command, which provides more robustness against buffer overflows or other security issues due to its usage of fork/exec model and handles signals better than system().
CommandRunner's constructor and destructor are not properly initialized.

The `CommandRunner` class in the utils.cpp file has a system call inside its constructor which could lead to command injection attacks if an attacker can control one of these calls or pass it as part of user input, leading them into executing arbitrary commands on their behalf.

The `setPassword` function in the CommandRunner class is using a string literal as an argument to set password. This can lead to security issues if this value could be manipulated by users or maliciously crafted inputs, leading to potential buffer overflows and other vulnerabilities such as command injection attacks (CVE-2014-6275).

The `allocateBuffer` function in the CommandRunner class returns a raw pointer, which may lead to unsafe ownership handling. This could potentially allow for buffer overruns and other issues related to memory management if not properly managed or freed after use by calling system(command). FIX: Ensure that all dynamically allocated buffers are correctly released using `free` function in the destructor of CommandRunner class, SEVERITY: medium
